entries.answer: Earth's atmosphere is the layer of gases surrounding Earth, dominated by nitrogen and oxygen.
Climate describes long-term statistical patterns of weather and environmental conditions.
Weather describes the short-term state of the atmosphere at a place and time.
The water cycle describes movement of water through evaporation, condensation, precipitation, infiltration and runoff.
Tectonic plates are large pieces of Earth's lithosphere that move relative to one another.
An earthquake is ground motion caused by a sudden release of energy in Earth's crust or mantle.
A volcano is a geological structure through which magma, gases or volcanic material can reach the surface.
A tsunami is a series of long ocean waves usually generated by displacement of a large volume of water.
An ocean is a major continuous body of salt water covering much of Earth's surface.
A continent is one of Earth's major landmass divisions.
Evaporation is the transition of a substance from liquid to gas at a surface.
Condensation is the transition of a substance from gas to liquid.
